name: In-app consent platforms (TCF/CMP)
plain: A consent screen the developer shows (in addition to the OS prompt) for EEA, UK and some US laws.
meaning: Recorded consent decides what ad SDKs may do. Since 2024 Google requires a certified CMP for ads in the EEA. On iOS it adds a second prompt beside ATT, which Italy called double consent.

android.store_policy: Google EU user consent policy; Play Families
android.api_surface: Google UMP SDK, TCF 2.2 strings in app storage

ios.store_policy: ATT remains separate; privacy manifest tracking flag
ios.note: Italy's regulator treats ATT plus a CMP as double consent.

limits.headline: Can show an extra consent screen on top of the phone prompt
limits.user_action: You see a Consent screen the first time you open the app, often in the EU or UK
can: Ask you to say yes or no to ads, analytics and sharing
Store your answer on the phone
Tell its ad tools what you agreed to
Show again later if you change your mind
cannot: Skip the screen when Google needs a certified one for EEA ads
Count as your consent if the answer is not recorded
Replace the phone's own prompt; on iPhone you may see two
limits.reach_label: Your choice, passed to the app

story.what_it_is: The extra consent screen an app shows, for privacy laws, on top of the phone's own prompt.
story.for_you: You see a screen asking you to accept or manage cookies and ad choices in an app, often before the app opens. Your answer is saved and sent to ad partners.
story.for_makers: Laws like GDPR require consent before personal ad data is used. Makers use a CMP so ad SDKs only do what the saved choice allows, and Google requires it for ads in the EEA.

use_cases.example: A news app asks you to consent to personalized ads before showing articles.
A free game shows a consent form at first launch, then loads ads based on your answer.
An ad SDK reads the saved consent string and serves non personalized ads when you say no.
A social app offers separate toggles for ads, analytics and personalization.
A retailer stores your consent so it can prove it asked, for audits.
A product team measures how many users accept and tunes the wording.

story.android_note: Android has no system consent screen. Apps use a CMP.
story.ios_note: On iOS the CMP appears beside the ATT prompt, which Apple allows if it is not misleading.

technical_bounds: Consent must precede SDK init in EEA

history.change: Certified CMP required for ads in EEA and UK (Jan 2024)
Italy fines Apple over double consent
